title: Starting on piano at house parties and joining Henry Allen at the Radio Cafe
summary: He learned piano at house parties, was tried out by Kid Howard's band, then hired by Henry Allen and Albert Martin for two years at the Radio Cafe.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: What instrument did you start on?

Well I started playing piano in house parties. And I went to rehearsal where Kid Howard was playing at a house party on barracks between Ramport and St. Claude. And Johnny Pradoz told Howard, say, well let's make a good piano player. He said try him in another key. So they kept on switching keys and I would follow them. They took my name and address. Well I played several jobs with them. And one day, Henry Allen was looking for a piano player, him and Albert Martin. And I was staying at 1450 St. Claude Street. And they came to my house. And they hired me to play at the Radio Cafe, which is at the corner from here.
Decatur and Tulip. On that side.
And I worked out there with them all about two years, maybe better than two years.
When you started on piano, did you have a piano at home to practice on? Take lessons?

No, I was just taking piano, you know, by going by different people's house like that. And I learned how to play the couple of numbers. And well piano players would skates then, they'd get jammed for parties, they would hire me, you know. And that's how I came out to the light. And after I got with them, well I got to follow music, and in later years, in 1927, 1928 like that, I'd taken to trumpet. Well I learned how to play trumpet a pretty good while. I got in the chamelea band playing piano. And after Wooden Joe got off the trumpet, he had taken sick, I played a couple of jobs in his place. Well Wooden Joe got in bed with the band, and he left. When he left I replaced him on trumpet.
